extracted.intended_audience: respondents, counsel, and patent practitioners involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and disposition of a Request for Reconsideration of a Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (reciprocal discipline), including requests for stay or modification, correction of errors in the Final Order, and setting the effective date of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability of 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c) to § 11.24 reciprocal discipline hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent requested reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c); however, 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c) is not applicable to reciprocal discipline hearings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests in reciprocal discipline matters should not be treated under § 11.56(c); instead the matter may be considered under the Director's plenary authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's plenary authority to consider reconsideration requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specific regulatory provision (e.g., § 11.56(c)) does not apply, the USPTO Director may consider a Request for Reconsideration under the Director's plenary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests may be considered and decided by the Director even if not brought under the inapplicable regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance standard for granting reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A Request for Reconsideration must present information that would have affected the basis for the original decision; arguments that are irrelevant to the basis for the decision do not provide sufficient basis for relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the order: the 2007 sealing order could not have affected Respondent's state of mind or the legal consequences of the pardon at the time he filled out his bar application in 2000; therefore the argument was irrelevant and insufficient to grant relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of later state-court sealing orders on prior disclosure/discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: A state order sealing records issued after the events at issue does not retroactively change the state of mind of the respondent or the legal consequences that existed at the time of earlier filings (e.g., a bar application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sealing order issued in 2007 could not alter the legal consequences or facts relevant to conduct or disclosures that occurred earlier (e.g., in 2000) or affect separate events in other jurisdictions (e.g., California).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of stay or penalty modification absent sufficient basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for a stay of a Final Order or modification of the penalty (e.g., downgrading status instead of suspension) will be denied if the requester does not present sufficient grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, the Request for Reconsideration seeking a stay and modification of the penalty was denied because the arguments offered did not justify the requested relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to correct clerical/terminology errors in Final Orders (errata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerical or wording errors in a Final Order may be corrected by errata (e.g., changing 'disbarred' to 'suspended' and 'disbarment' to 'suspension' on specified lines of the Final Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order granted correction of three occurrences on page 15 and attached errata specifying the exact textual changes and locations (page and line numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resetting effective commencement date of suspension by agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree that if a suspension is maintained, the effective commencement date of the suspension period will be reset to the date of an order issued in response to a Request for Reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, by telephone agreement, the effective commencement date for the six-month suspension was reset to commence as of the date of the Director's Order addressing the Request for Reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's obligations to comply with disciplinary duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a suspension is imposed, the respondent remains responsible to comply with duties set out in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and § 11.60 as specified in the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly resets the commencement date for the six-month suspension 'as well as Respondent's responsibility to comply with his duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and 11.60 as set out in the Final Order of April 23, 2009.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate of service requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.11 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision includes a Certificate of Service certifying that the Decision on Request for Reconsideration was mailed by first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service (mailing and certificate) to the address provided under § 11.11 is documented and required for notice of the Order.
